meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid bijural federal state: Quebec private law, company law and partnership law are civil law (Civil Code of Quebec, CQLR c CCQ-1991); federal public law, criminal law and tax procedure are common law; the Quebec Limited Partnership Act (CQLR c S-2.1) is a provincial civil-law statute.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA), in force 1 Jul 2020
Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisionally applied since 21 Sep 2017
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), in force 30 Dec 2018
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA), signed 9 Sep 2012 (not yet in force)
Canada-Philippines Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement, in force 1 Nov 1996
Canada-China Income Tax Convention (1986), as amended by the 2009 Protocol

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA) and FINTRAC Regulations; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, s 462.31; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2017, c 21; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1 (public beneficial-ownership register operative since 31 Mar 2023); Limited Partnership Act, CQLR c S-2.1; Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, r 1; Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and register of directors/shareholders of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or registered agent of the general partner's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued in the document's country of origin (in force for Canada since 11 Jan 2024); for non-Convention emerging-market jurisdictions, consular legalization at the nearest Canadian visa office

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or certified copy of registration of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the general partner's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable, followed by certified French translation for filing with the Registraire des entreprises

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport and proof of residential address of every ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) holding 25% or more of the partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus sworn French translation where the UBO resides outside Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the Quebec incorporation agent and registered-office service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Quebec notary or foreign notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization of foreign signatures; the instrument is filed in the enterprise's legal publicity file with the Registraire des entreprises

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference and source-of-funds confirmation letter for capital contributions to the limited partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Deposit-taking institution maintaining the contributor's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original letter countersigned by the bank's compliance officer; apostille recommended but not strictly required for the enhanced KYC file

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, UBOs, directors and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List (1267/1988/1989), Global Affairs Canada consolidated autonomous sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists where USD settlement or US counter-parties are involved, and commercial global PEP databases. Enhanced ongoing monitoring applies given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced cash-on-delivery profile and cross-border remittance rails (Airwallex and local logistics remittance).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - online name reservation service (Service de reservation de nom), portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, s 21: the enterprise name must be in French; a name containing non-French words or non-Latin characters is registrable only together with an approved French version; non-Roman scripts (e.g., Mandarin characters) must be transliterated into Latin script; the French version governs legal identification.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANK / BANQUE / TRUST (federal OSFI or AMF authorization required)
UNIVERSITY / COLLEGE (Ministere de l'Enseignement superieur consent required)
ENGINEER / INGENIEUR (Ordre des ingenieurs du Quebec permit required)
LAWYER / AVOCAT / LEGAL (Barreau du Quebec authorization required)
ROYAL / GOVERNMENT / MUNICIPAL (tokens implying Crown or public authority, ministerial approval required)
QUEBEC / CANADA (use implying government sponsorship, prior ministerial authorization required)
MONEY SERVICES BUSINESS / EXCHANGE (AMF registration under the Money-Services Businesses Act required for COD remittance activities)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation cannot be extended after the 90-day window; the applicant must file a new reservation and pay the fee again. Upon rejection: (i) obtain the written consent of the conflicting name holder or of the competent ministry for a sensitive token; (ii) re-file with a new distinctive or geographic element and the legal-form suffix S.E.C. (societe en commandite); (iii) file a written application for review with the Registraire within 30 days of the refusal notice under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; (iv) seek judicial review at the Superior Court of Quebec under articles 529-555 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible where the registered address is a physical place in Quebec staffed during business hours for service of documents; a post-office box alone is statutorily inadequate for the Registraire des entreprises and Revenu Quebec. A virtual-office or registered-agent arrangement satisfies the head-office address requirement for mail-order and cash-on-delivery e-commerce limited partnerships.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 20% annual probability for the Medium_Risk_Enhanced COD profile; unannounced inspections may be conducted by Revenu Quebec under the Tax Administration Act (CQLR c A-6.002) and by FINTRAC for regulated reporting entities relying on the LP's cash-collection flow.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of the Registraire des entreprises (CQLR c P-44.1; CAD 33 per reservation)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of the Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership (societe en commandite)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified copy of the registration file and attestation of registration for merchant/bank account opening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for certified copies and attestations (approximately CAD 30 per document set)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille and consular legalization of foreign corporate and UBO documentation bundle (5 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public; Ministere de la Justice du Quebec (apostille service); Global Affairs Canada and Canadian missions abroad
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rates for Quebec notarial services plus CAD 25 per apostille under the Hague Convention (in force for Canada since 11 Jan 2024); consular fees where emerging-market documents require legalization

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of the partnership agreement skeleton, general partner corporate documents and UBO identity documents (Charter of the French Language compliance)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator, member of the Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interpretes agrees du Quebec (OTTIAQ)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (CAD 250-300 for the core bundle); statutory requirement under CQLR c C-11, s 21 and the Regulation respecting legal publicity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and service-of-process address in Quebec - first year (virtual office/registered agent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed registered-agent or virtual-office provider in Montreal or Quebec City
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of CAD 500 per annum for a staffed commercial address with document forwarding

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the Quebec limited partnership agreement (contrat de societe) and initial resolutions of the general partner

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Enhanced KYC/AML bundle: PEP and sanctions screening of all UBOs, general partner and authorized signatories; UBO documentation review and adverse-media report

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), Book Five, Title Three, Partnership, arts. 2186-2244, and limited partnership arts. 2236-2243; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 21-37 (immatriculation, annual declaration, and register updates); Regulation respecting the fees and tariffs of the Registraire des entreprises, CQLR c P-44.1, r. 5; Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), Services Québec, 510 boulevard Charest Est, Québec (Québec), G1K 8W9.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation of a société en commandite (Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no statutorily mandated escrow account apply to a Quebec limited partnership. Contributions are fixed freely in the limited partnership agreement. For this engagement, the agreed initial capital contribution is CAD 100,000, to be deposited into the LP's Quebec operating account or Airwallex settlement wallet; any cash-on-delivery courier escrow is contractual security, not a statutory requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED: (1) The General Partner, acting as managing partner, accepts the capital subscription of the initial limited partners, as set out in Schedule A of the Limited Partnership Agreement, totaling CAD One Hundred Thousand, and directs the maintenance of the capital and escrow records for Cash-on-Delivery settlement. (2) The registered office is established at [address], Quebec, and the Registraire des entreprises is instructed to file the Declaration of Registration. (3) [Name] is appointed General Manager and Chief Compliance Officer, authorized to open banking and payment accounts, including Airwallex, and to engage local logistics remittance providers. (4) The officers shall execute all registrations and tax filings with Revenu Québec and the Canada Revenue Agency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Reservation with the Quebec Enterprise Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec, online name reservation module (Services Québec portal).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name reservation request containing the proposed English and French trade names of the limited partnership, each bearing the compulsory legal descriptor société en commandite or L.P. Verify availability against the Quebec enterprise register; for a cross-border COD e-commerce brand, also submit a complementary nominative mark if the LP will operate under a commercial brand. The reservation is valid for 60 days and may be renewed once for an additional 60 days. The reserved name must be used in the registration declaration filed at Step 3.
required_dossiers: Proposed French and English partnership names
Statement of principal activity (ISIC 4791 / NAICS 454110, mail-order retail with cash-on-delivery settlement)
Legal identification of the general partner and its Quebec enterprise number, if any
Written mandate or power of attorney from the non-resident limited partners to the forming agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusion with an existing enterprise, file an amended reservation adding a distinctive element or submit a consent letter from the prior name holder. If the refusal concerns linguistic conformity, adapt the name to the Charter of the French Language and resubmit within 30 days without loss of filing priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement and Adoption of Governance Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private contracting by the partners; optional notarization by a notary of the Chambre des notaires du Québec.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Limited Partnership Agreement (LPA) in writing, identifying the general partner, all limited partners, capital commitments, profit and loss sharing ratios, management powers, COD settlement waterfall through Airwallex and local logistics remittance, and the restriction on limited partners participating in management. Adopt the First Board Resolution of the general partner, establish the statutory registered office address in Quebec, appoint the general manager, chief compliance officer, and agent for service, and create the partnership minute book containing the LPA, resolutions, partner register, and capital account statements.
required_dossiers: Duly executed Limited Partnership Agreement
First Board Resolution of the General Partner
Certificate of status or equivalent record of the general partner
Consent letter or lease evidencing the registered office address in Quebec
Acceptance form of the agent for service of process
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar later queries the registered office or the agent, file a corrected amending declaration online within the statutory 15-day response period; if a limited partner is found to have taken part in management, that partner must be removed from management with retroactive effect or the partner's limited liability may be challenged under CCQ art. 2240.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Registration and Issuance of the Quebec Enterprise Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec, online filing platform (Registre des entreprises website).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Déclaration d'immatriculation online using the reserved name, providing the LP's legal form (société en commandite), registered office address in Quebec, general partner particulars, names and addresses of limited partners, and principal business activity (mail-order retail with cash-on-delivery settlement). Pay the CAD 38 online registration fee. Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and publishes the declaration, which confers the public notice effect and triggers the annual declaration obligation under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.
required_dossiers: Certificate of name reservation
Completed online registration questionnaire
Identification and enterprise number of the general partner
Schedule of limited partners and their contributions
Credit card or INTERAC payment authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is refused for incomplete partner identification or missing documents, use the online resubmission function within 30 days; if the refusal arises from a defective name, obtain a new reservation or a consent letter. Late registration is cured by immediate filing together with payment of the late-filing penalty and a written request for penalty remission to the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registrar Onboarding with Revenu Québec and the Canada Revenue Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (TPS/TVQ and Quebec tax accounts) and Canada Revenue Agency (Business Number and GST/HST).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NEQ, register the limited partnership with Revenu Québec for the Quebec Sales Tax (TVQ) and GST (TPS) accounts, mandatory for retail sales into Quebec, and file CTRCT/Preliminary data. Register with the CRA for a federal Business Number and GST/HST account where applicable. If fulfillment staff will be hired in Quebec, register for a CRA payroll account and with the CNESST for occupational health coverage. Submit the LPA and capital schedule to establish pass-through tax classification and any Quebec withholding requirements applicable to non-resident limited partners.
required_dossiers: NEQ registration certificate
Executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Identification details of non-resident limited partners
Estimated first-year Queebec and Canadian taxable sales
Authorization forms for tax representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Revenu Québec contests the LP's pass-through status or imposes a withholding obligation on distributions to non-resident limited partners, submit a reasoned technical memorandum with the LPA within 30 days and, if unresolved, apply to the Revenu Québec ruling service for an advance income tax ruling or file a Notice of Objection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Cash-on-Delivery Payment Rail Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (NEQ documentary basis); Schedule I Canadian bank or Airwallex; local logistics remittance partners under AMF AML supervision.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a Canadian Dollar and US Dollar operating account in the LP's name presenting the NEQ certificate, the LPA, the First Board Resolution, and the partner register. Configure the COD settlement rails: Airwallex for multi-currency receivables and local logistics remittance for cash collection by parcel couriers. Complete the medium-risk enhanced KYB package including the beneficial ownership schedule of limited partners and general partner, and execute the AML/CFT onboarding representation that COD cash flows will be reconciled daily and suspicious transactions reported to FINTRAC.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration (NEQ)
Limited Partnership Agreement and First Board Resolution
Register of limited partners with beneficial ownership breakdown
Proof of registered office in Quebec
AML/KYB questionnaire for medium-risk cash-collection model
Airwallex merchant onboarding application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or Airwallex rejects the LP due to the cash-on-delivery model, provide the legal opinion confirming pass-through status and the AML control framework, request an internal compliance review, or pivot to a secondary payment facilitator approved by the monetary authority while maintaining the same reconciliation controls.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Annual Declaration and Continuous Post-Formation Compliance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec; Revenu Québec; Canada Revenue Agency; FINTRAC.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before the first anniversary of registration, file the annual declaration online updating the registered office, general and limited partners, and the principal activity. Maintain the Quebec minute book with the LPA, resolutions, partner register, capital account statements, and COD settlement records. Prepare the LP's first fiscal-period pass-through tax returns and GST/TVQ returns, and implement the FINTRAC AML program with daily monitoring of cash-on-delivery collections through Airwallex and local logistics remittance accounts.
required_dossiers: Annual declaration form and payment
Updated register of partners and capital account schedule
GST/TVQ return draft and supporting sales data
AML transaction monitoring log and exception report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the LP is struck from the register for failure to file the annual declaration, file a late declaration within 30 days with the applicable penalty or apply for reinstatement under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; for tax penalties, file a voluntary disclosure with Revenu Québec or the CRA to seek penalty and interest relief.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 4791 mail-order retail with cash-on-delivery settlement is classified as commercial digital commerce and is not subject to Quebec industrial licensing. A municipal general business permit would be required only if a physical fulfillment warehouse is subsequently leased.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating or manufacturing license is mandated for this activity; the operative authorization is the declaration of registration and the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) issued by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP), Gouvernement du Québec.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity falls outside the mandatory environmental impact assessment and authorization categories of Section 22 of the Environment Quality Act, CQLR c Q-2, because no industrial facility, stationary combustion equipment, or effluent-generating process is operated by a mail-order COD enterprise at formation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable at the formation stage. If a fulfillment warehouse is later operated: wastewater discharges will be subject to municipal sewer use by-laws, residual materials handling under the Regulation respecting residual materials, CQLR c Q-2, r. 35, and greenhouse-gas reporting under the Regulation respecting mandatory reporting of certain emissions of contaminants, CQLR c Q-2, r. 15, if the annual CO2-equivalent threshold is met.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable to the office-only formation stage. Before commissioning any fulfillment centre, the LP must obtain: (i) fire safety certification under the Fire Safety Code, RLRQ c S-3.1, r. 9, and the applicable municipal fire prevention by-law; (ii) structural and occupancy clearance from the municipal building inspectorate; and (iii) CNESST registration and workplace health and safety clearance under the Act respecting occupational health and safety, CQLR c S-2.1, prior to hiring material-handling staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — Business Registration Online portal (www.canada.ca) and CRA My Business Account; Quebec sub-authority: Revenu Québec (CLIC portal) and Registraire des entreprises du Québec (NEQ issuance)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-resident partner establishing a Quebec limited partnership (société en commandite) must: (1) register the LP with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, obtaining the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ); (2) apply for the CRA Business Number (BN) via Form RC1 (Business Number Request), selecting the GST/HST account (RT), partnership income account (RC), and import/export account (RM) as needed; (3) register separately for QST with Revenu Québec, which administers GST and QST in Quebec under a single-administration agreement; (4) file Form T5013 (Partnership Information Return) annually if the LP carries on business in Canada or earns Canadian-source income. No minimum capital contribution is required; non-resident ownership is permitted, but a representative for service of process may be required. The LP's pass-through status is automatic upon formation; the BN serves as the sole federal tax identification number for the partnership.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — The Quebec LP is fiscally transparent under the Income Tax Act (ITA): the partnership does not pay income tax; each partner is taxed on its distributive share. Canadian-resident partners are taxed on worldwide income; non-resident partners are taxable under ITA s. 2(3) and Part I / Part XIV on Canadian-source business income attributable to the LP's Canadian business. No Quebec tax-exempt zone applies. For GST/HST and QST purposes, the LP is a distinct 'registrant person' separate from its partners and must account for tax itself.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box election or hybrid-entity classification; pass-through treatment is mandatory for income tax. Available statutory elections include: (i) non-calendar partnership fiscal period under ITA s. 249.1, permitted only where no partner is a 'specified member' (partnerships with Canadian-resident partners are effectively forced to a December 31 year-end); (ii) GST/HST Quick Method election for qualifying small suppliers whose annual worldwide taxable revenues do not exceed CAD 400,000; (iii) no hybrid-mismatch election is available — the hybrid mismatch rules (ITA ss. 94.1–94.3) operate by disallowance, not registration; (iv) the ETA s. 156 closely related corporation election is not available to partnerships.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax under the Quebec Sales Tax Act); Quebec administers both GST and QST via Revenu Québec
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — a supplier becomes a mandatory registrant when worldwide taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated supplies) exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; the same CAD 30,000 threshold applies for QST in Quebec. Once exceeded, registration is mandatory effective from the date the threshold was surpassed. Non-resident suppliers making taxable supplies in Canada (including digital or mail-order sales) are subject to the same CAD 30,000 threshold under the place-of-supply rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory continuous-control invoicing regime is in force in Canada or Quebec as of 2025. The Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing initiative has adopted the Peppol framework on a voluntary basis, with production availability targeted for 2026. Mandatory electronic filing applies: GST/HST returns must be filed via GST/HST NETFILE (CRA) and QST returns via Revenu Québec's CLIC platform. No API-based pre-clearance or CRA/Revenu Québec validation of individual invoices is required; paper or PDF invoices remain legally valid if they meet ETA s. 223 record-keeping requirements (six years' retention).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods (including mail-order and COD parcels) are zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V of the Excise Tax Act (ETA) if the supplier exports the goods or delivers them to a common carrier for export to a non-resident purchaser within 60 days of the time of supply, and property in the goods passes outside Canada. Services supplied to non-residents are zero-rated only where not performed in Canada or performed wholly outside Canada; services relating to Canadian real property or tangible personal property do not qualify. QST zero-rating mirrors the GST under the Quebec Sales Tax Act. COD settlement through a foreign logistics partner or convergent payment rail (e.g., Airwallex) does not disqualify zero-rating, provided the vendor's records evidence delivery to a foreign address and that the goods were not re-delivered into Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Canadian Export Declaration (electronic export reporting via Canada Border Services Agency, G13/CAARS confirmation, required for exports exceeding CAD 2,500 or regulated goods)
Commercial invoice / sales contract naming the foreign COD buyer
Bill of Lading or parcel consignment waybill evidencing Canadian consignor and foreign consignee
Inward Remittance Certificate equivalent — SWIFT MT103, Airwallex export collection statement, or the local logistics partner's COD remittance report
Packing list and shipping log matching the customs export declaration
Proof of non-resident status of the buyer (foreign billing/shipping address, IP or geo-location evidence for COD verification)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess within the normal four-year period from the filing due date; the period extends to eight years for large businesses (annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 500,000) and is unlimited where misrepresentation, fraud, or willful default is established. Export zero-rating claims are scrutinized for proof of export within the 60-day rule and non-return of goods into Canada; failure to substantiate results in retroactive clawback of the 0% rate and assessment of 14.975% GST/QST, plus interest under ETA s. 280 and the QSTA. Civil penalties for false statements in returns are the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the net tax sought to be evaded (ETA s. 285.1); false GST/QST rebate or refund claims attract additional penalties of CAD 500 to CAD 10,000. Criminal prosecution for willful evasion under ETA s. 327.02 may result in fines up to CAD 500,000 and imprisonment up to five years. Although the 180-day FX repatriation deadline is a compliance covenant of the Airwallex/local logistics remittance rails rather than an ETA statutory requirement, late or undocumented repatriation may trigger Part XIII withholding exposure where the non-resident logistics partner is deemed to earn Canadian-source service income.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada; foreign-exchange transaction reporting and anti-money-laundering supervision also involve the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), the Canada Border Services Agency for cross-border currency reporting, the Canada Revenue Agency for tax administration, and the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) for Quebec-regulated derivatives and financial-market activities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada has a freely convertible Canadian dollar and no general exchange-control regime. Current-account payments, including trade payments, service fees, interest, dividends, partnership distributions, and other ordinary commercial remittances, are generally permitted without central-bank pre-approval. Capital-account transactions, including capital contributions, loans, acquisitions, guarantees, and repatriation of invested capital, are also generally unrestricted, subject to corporate authority, partnership-agreement terms, sanctions, tax compliance, anti-money-laundering controls, beneficial-ownership verification, transfer-pricing requirements, withholding-tax obligations, thin-capitalization rules where applicable, and lender or investor restrictions. A Quebec limited partnership may distribute cash subject to its partnership agreement, solvency considerations, creditor claims, applicable tax reporting, and confirmation that the distribution is not a disguised payment for an unlawful or restricted transaction. Canadian financial institutions may require source-of-funds evidence, tax residency information, foreign tax forms, contracts, invoices, customs records, and a clear economic rationale before processing large or unusual cross-border transfers. There is no general profit-remittance approval or mandatory conversion into Canadian dollars.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada does not generally require exporters to surrender export proceeds to a Canadian bank, convert foreign-currency receipts, or repatriate receipts within a statutory period. Export proceeds may ordinarily be retained in foreign-currency accounts or received through payment processors, subject to contractual banking terms, sanctions screening, tax reporting, accounting records, and anti-money-laundering controls. Cross-border currency or monetary-instrument movements of CAD 10,000 or more in a single transaction or related transactions within the applicable reporting framework must be reported through the prescribed Canada Border Services Agency process when physically imported into or exported from Canada; financial institutions also have separate FINTRAC reporting obligations for reportable transactions. There is no mandatory export-proceeds conversion ratio. Foreign-currency revenue remains reportable for Canadian income-tax and financial-reporting purposes using applicable exchange-rate and recognition rules.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for payment collection, foreign-exchange conversion, supplier payments, and treasury workflow, but not a complete substitute for a Canadian deposit-taking bank. Airwallex and comparable foreign electronic-money institutions or payment-service providers may provide multi-currency collection and payout services only within their licensing perimeter, contractual corridors, and correspondent-banking arrangements. Client-money safeguarding or segregation does not necessarily provide Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation protection and may not constitute a Canadian operating deposit account. The provider may decline cash-on-delivery proceeds, marketplace flows, emerging-market counterparties, high chargeback exposure, cash-intensive activity, or unexplained third-party collections. The limited partnership should maintain a Canadian bank as its primary operating and reserve account, use payment accounts only for documented commercial flows, reconcile processor settlements to orders and delivery records, and avoid personal accounts, nominee accounts, undisclosed sub-merchants, and unsupported third-party settlement instructions. Canadian anti-money-laundering, sanctions, consumer-protection, privacy, tax, payment-service, and foreign-licensing requirements may apply depending on the actual activities and customer location.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian law does not impose a universal statutory requirement that all directors or partners appear physically at a branch. Remote onboarding may be available for eligible entities after electronic identity verification and document authentication. In practice, a limited partnership with non-resident partners, foreign controllers, emerging-market counterparties, cash-on-delivery collections, payment intermediaries, or unusual transaction corridors may be required to attend a video interview, provide notarized or apostilled documents, use a Canadian authorized signatory, or complete branch onboarding. Banks may impose their own presence requirements and may refuse remote opening where identity, control, source of funds, tax residency, business purpose, or expected activity cannot be independently verified. A limited partnership should identify its general partner, all beneficial owners and controlling persons, authorized signatories, tax residents, and persons exercising effective control; limited partners should be disclosed where required by the institution's ownership and control thresholds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partners, foreign general partner, opaque ownership chain, nominee arrangements, or inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owners and persons exercising control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified partnership agreement and amendments; Quebec registration or business-number records; general-partner constitutional documents; ownership chart through each corporate layer to natural persons; passports and residential-address evidence for partners, controllers, directors, and signatories; incumbency or authority certificates; beneficial-ownership declaration; tax-residency self-certifications; written explanation of governance and signing authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-on-delivery model, logistics remittance, cash-intensive settlement, rapid pass-through of customer funds, or high volume of small payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business model memorandum; customer journey and funds-flow diagram; logistics-provider agreements; delivery and collection procedures; payment processor agreements; settlement reports; order, invoice, delivery, return, refund, and chargeback records; expected monthly volume and transaction-size analysis; cash-handling controls; customer identification and sanctions-screening procedures; reconciliation policy; independent audit or control report where available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Emerging-market counterparties, high-risk countries, sanctioned jurisdictions, politically exposed persons, adverse media, or unexplained payment corridors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country and counterparty risk matrix; sanctions and PEP screening methodology; customer and supplier due-diligence files; beneficial-ownership evidence; commercial contracts; invoices; shipping and customs documentation; proof of goods or services; end-use and end-user statements; enhanced due-diligence approvals; escalation and transaction-monitoring procedures; documented rationale for each higher-risk corridor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming capital, shareholder or partner loans, related-party funding, or transfers from an account not held in the legal entity's name.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed contribution or loan agreement; partnership resolutions; lender or investor identity and beneficial-ownership documents; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; bank statements; audited financial statements; tax returns or tax assessments where appropriate; purpose-of-payment narrative; capital-account ledger; repayment and interest schedule; confirmation that the remitter is contractually entitled to fund the entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch among industry code, website, stated business purpose, payment volumes, and actual transaction activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current business plan; website and platform evidence; supplier and logistics contracts; product catalogue; projected cash-flow statement; customer geography; expected currencies; average and peak transaction values; transaction-volume assumptions; management biographies; explanation of the ISIC 4791 and NAICS 454110 classification; prompt notification protocol for material business changes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of offshore electronic-money institutions, payment aggregators, marketplaces, or third-party collection accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provider licensing and regulatory-status evidence; executed service agreement; account-ownership confirmation; safeguarding or segregation terms; settlement waterfall; processor due-diligence report; transaction-level reconciliation; chargeback and refund controls; bank statements; explanation of why the account is commercially necessary; prohibition on commingling customer and partnership funds unless legally and contractually permitted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected foreign-exchange activity without a demonstrable underlying commercial exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Currency exposure policy; forecast receipts and payables by currency; supplier invoices; customer contracts; hedge-accounting or valuation policy; approved trading authorities; confirmation that derivatives are used for risk management rather than speculative dealing; board or partner approval; counterparty-credit and collateral arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency uncertainty, failure to provide Canadian tax identification, or inconsistent foreign tax forms.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Canada Revenue Agency business-number and program-account records where applicable; partnership tax filings; T5013-related records where applicable; GST/HST and Quebec tax registrations where applicable; residency certificates; FATCA and Common Reporting Standard self-certifications; partner tax-residency schedule; withholding-tax analysis; written explanation of pass-through taxation and allocation methodology.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual cash deposits, structured transactions, unexplained third-party refunds, or rapid movement between bank and payment accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cash and settlement policy; deposit logs; point-of-sale or courier records; source-of-cash evidence; daily reconciliation; refund authorization matrix; customer and order-level reports; exception reports; transaction-monitoring alerts and disposition records; internal compliance training; independent review of suspicious-transaction escalation procedures.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route partner contributions, equity-equivalent funding, and partner loans from an account in the documented investor or lender name to the Quebec limited partnership's Canadian operating or designated capital account through SWIFT or another bank-approved international wire channel. Use an accurate payment purpose, such as partner capital contribution, partner loan, intercompany loan, or settlement of a documented commercial invoice; do not label capital funding as trade revenue or use an unrelated third-party remitter. Include the legal entity name, Canadian account number, institution and transit details, SWIFT/BIC, registered address, partnership or loan reference, and remitter identity. Retain wire messages, contribution or loan agreements, resolutions, source-of-funds evidence, and ledger entries. The receiving bank may request confirmation of the source, ultimate beneficial owner, expected use, and tax treatment before release. Reconcile foreign-currency receipts at the bank statement level and document the exchange rate, fees, and Canadian-dollar accounting value. For physical currency or monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or more entering Canada, complete the applicable CBSA declaration. Apply sanctions screening, FINTRAC controls, transfer-pricing documentation for related-party funding, and withholding-tax analysis for interest or other cross-border payments.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use Canadian bank accounts for supplier, logistics, customs, platform, refund, and other documented trade payments. SWIFT MT103 or the successor message format may be used for international customer-credit transfers, subject to the bank's current messaging standards; include complete ordering-customer, beneficiary, intermediary-bank, invoice, and purpose information. Use commercial letters of credit, documentary collections, open-account transfers, or card and payment-provider rails according to counterparty risk and the underlying sale or purchase terms. For a commercial letter of credit, define issuing and confirming banks, beneficiary, presentation documents, Incoterms, shipment evidence, inspection requirements, insurance, expiry, and discrepancy procedures. Maintain invoice, purchase order, logistics, customs, proof-of-delivery, refund, and settlement records. Screen beneficiaries, banks, vessels, goods, countries, and counterparties for Canadian and applicable foreign sanctions. Do not split payments to avoid reporting or screening, pay undisclosed third parties, or transmit funds without a bona fide commercial or financing basis. Verify GST/HST, Quebec sales-tax, customs, withholding, and non-resident service-provider consequences before payment.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized Canadian bank or appropriately regulated dealer, supported by documented forecast or contracted currency exposure and approved dealing limits.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or jurisdictions where physical delivery is restricted or impracticable, subject to counterparty eligibility, applicable Canadian securities and derivatives rules, settlement documentation, and a genuine hedging purpose.

Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity, settlement-date management, or currency funding, subject to documented commercial exposure, counterparty credit limits, collateral terms, and accounting treatment.

Currency options, collars, and purchased option structures may be available through an authorized dealer, but should be limited to approved hedging purposes, with clear premium, valuation, break-cost, collateral, and suitability analysis.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps may be used for material foreign-currency financing exposures where the entity can satisfy dealer credit, documentation, suitability, valuation, and collateral requirements.

Hedging documentation should identify the exposure, currency, notional, tenor, hedge ratio, counterparty, approval authority, settlement account, valuation method, termination rights, and accounting or tax treatment. A Quebec entity and its dealers should assess applicable AMF requirements, Canadian securities legislation, derivatives reporting rules, trade-repository obligations, eligible-counterparty standards, and any dealer-specific documentation before execution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration to the Registre des entreprises du Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to CAD 500; repeated non-filing may trigger administrative dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the limited partnership exceeds Quebec enterprise size thresholds (e.g., revenue exceeding CAD 1,000,000 or 50 employees)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual declaration to REJ confirms partners and reports any ownership or partner transfers

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general corporate rate (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%). The CA_LP is fiscally transparent; no entity-level tax is imposed, and each partner is taxed on allocated income at their applicable rates.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction: combined 14% federal (9%) + Quebec (5%) on up to CAD 500,000 of active business income allocated to a Canadian-controlled private corporate partner; SR&ED refundable credits (federal 35%; Quebec 30%); no automatic tax holiday for ISIC 4791 mail-order retail.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T5013 Partnership Information Return filed electronically via CRA EFILE or NETFILE for businesses.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than 5 months after the partnership fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end: due May 31 of the following year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership legal name and CRA business number (BN, RP account).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact registered legal name; ensure the BN is activated for the partnership and the required Quebec registration is current.
A non-resident partner must report consistently with the partnership's chosen fiscal year-end; no separate Canadian year-end election is available to the LP.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenues and expenses by source, including mail-order e-commerce and COD settlement commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Canadian-source sales gross proceeds; deduct logistics and payment-processing fees only where CRA-allowable and supported by contemporaneous documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of net income or loss to each partner, with percentage shares.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify non-resident partners and their share of Canadian-source income; amounts distributable to non-residents trigger Part XIII and Quebec 12% withholding obligations.
Use NAICS 2022 code 454110 (Electronic Shopping and Mail-Order Houses); inconsistent codes may trigger CRA business-purpose reviews.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T5013 filing: CAD 25 per day (minimum CAD 100) up to CAD 2,500; gross negligence or knowing false statements: CAD 100 per slip plus s. 163(2) penalty of 50% of the understated tax; criminal prosecution under s. 239 can add fines up to 200% of tax evaded.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Provincial: TP-600 Partnership Return filed via Revenu Québec's secure 'Echange de fichiers' portal (mon dossier d'entreprise).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than 6 months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., December 31 year-end: due June 30 of the following year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership legal name and Revenu Québec (NR) registration number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An LP carrying on business in Quebec must hold a valid NR account and disclose all non-resident partners' Quebec residency status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business revenue attributable to Quebec, including COD sales to Quebec consumers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Quebec attribution rules; revenue from Quebec customers is generally taxable in Quebec if the LP has a permanent establishment or solicits orders in Quebec.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of income to each partner; issue RL-15 slips.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each non-resident partner, calculate Quebec-source allocable income and apply the proportional reduction of the 12% Quebec withholding where a tax treaty applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late TP-600: CAD 25 per day (minimum CAD 100) up to CAD 2,500; failure to file: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month (maximum 12 months); willful omission: 50% penalty plus interest; criminal fines up to CAD 2,500 under the Tax Administration Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate partners must also file: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and Quebec CO-17, via EFILE / Revenu Québec's secure file transfer.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Both due no later than 6 months after the corporate fiscal year-end; balance-due payable 3 months after year-end (2 months for non-CCPCs).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership income allocated from T5013 / RL-15.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners must report allocated Canadian-source business income and may claim treaty-relief only where a Canadian permanent establishment exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Eligible capital dividends or foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits cannot be claimed for the Quebec 12% withholding unless a treaty allows; maintain NR4/T5013 records for the refund application.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T2/CO-17: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month (maximum 12 months); repeated failure: 10% plus 2% per month (maximum 20 months); Quebec mirrors the federal framework.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 37% combined statutory on dividends paid to non-residents of Canada by a payer resident in Quebec (federal Part XIII 25% + Quebec Taxation Act s. 1041.0.1 additional 12%).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: (1) Obtain a certificate of residence from the home-state tax authority (CRA Form NR301 serves for federal; Revenu Québec accepts the certificate for the provincial 12% levy). (2) Deliver the certificate to the Quebec payer before the payment date. (3) The payer applies the treaty-reduced rate to the federal Part XIII and proportionally reduces the Quebec 12% levy (Quebec rate = 12% × treaty federal rate ÷ 25%). (4) Retain the certificate and supporting tax-residence evidence for six years. (5) Where full tax was withheld, the non-resident files a federal NR7-R refund application and a corresponding Revenu Québec claim within two years of the end of the calendar year.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: federal Part XIII 25% plus Quebec 12% on royalties and on non-arm's length participating debt interest; arm's length interest is exempt from Part XIII. Typical treaty rates: Canada-US royalties 10%, interest up to 15%; Canada-UK royalties 10%, interest 10%; Quebec 12% is proportionally reduced under the same treaty formula.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File (RC5107): mandatory for fiscal years beginning after 2022 when total cross-border non-arm's length transactions exceed CAD 5,000,000. Master File: required when such transactions exceed CAD 100,000,000. T106 information return: required for reportable transactions exceeding CAD 1,000,000 in a taxation year. Country-by-Country Report: required for MNEs with group revenue of at least CAD 1.06 billion (EUR 750 million).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada applies no UAE-style ESR. However, non-resident LPs must demonstrate a permanent establishment (DTA Article V) and real business substance to access treaty benefits. The GAAR (federal Income Tax Act s. 245; Quebec Taxation Act s. 1079.12), the 'carrying on business in Canada' test (s. 253), and CRA substance reviews may re-characterize a shell LP that has no employees, premises, or independent decision-making in Quebec.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of COD e-commerce revenues sourced from Quebec customers; falsification of books; wilful participation in a fictitious partnership arrangement to conceal taxable Canadian business income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of 50% of the tax avoided plus arrears interest; criminal conviction under ITA s. 239 and Quebec TAA s. 72: fine of up to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment up to 5 years (indictable).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers who directed, authorized, or acquiesced in the evasion are jointly and severally liable for the corporate penalties; personal bankruptcy does not discharge these debts; travel bans and extradition can be ordered under tax-treaty mutual assistance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Quebec LP with no employees, no premises, no bank account, and no business substance, used solely to invoice mail-order sales and divert profits offshore to a zero-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR re-characterization and denial of the fiscal transparency of the LP; reassessment of the full 37% withholding on all repatriated amounts plus interest and penalties up to 50%; Quebec GAAR penalty and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil under common-law agency or sham doctrines; general partners are personally liable for the full tax debt of the LP; directors of the corporate general partner face civil restitution and potential criminal prosecution for forgery of documentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold Part XIII and Quebec 12%
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits, dividends, royalties, or management fees to non-resident partners or related foreign entities without withholding the federal 25% Part XIII tax and the additional 12% Quebec levy.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The full unwithheld amount becomes collectible from the payer under ITA s. 227(8) and Quebec TAA; penalty of 10% of the amount not withheld (s. 227(9)) plus daily interest on arrears; Quebec adds a 15% penalty on unreported withholdable amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are jointly and severally liable under ITA s. 227.1 and Quebec TAA s. 278 for all unremitted withholdings, including interest and penalties; this liability survives bankruptcy (super-priority claim) and can trigger personal travel bans during collection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare contemporaneous Local File/Master File and T106 schedules for COD logistics, payment gateway, and marketing fees paid to related non-resident service providers at non-arm's length markups.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 10% of the net transfer-pricing adjustment (minimum CAD 5,000) under ITA s. 247(3) and Quebec Taxation Act s. 1299.1; CRA may reassess beyond the normal three-year limitation period when transfer-pricing adjustments exceed the specified threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically liable, but involvement in the preparation of false documentation attracts the 50% gross-negligence penalty (s. 163(2)) and criminal liability under s. 239; penalties are uninsurable and non-dischargeable in bankruptcy.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving third-party logistics remittance settlements for cash-on-delivery sales without an AML compliance program, without reporting large cash transactions (CAD 10,000 or more), and without suspicious-transaction reports to FINTRAC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 2,000,000 per violation for enterprises under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; criminal money-laundering conviction: unlimited court-discretion fines and imprisonment up to 14 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers, directors, and partners who directed or authorized the non-compliance face personal criminal liability (PCMLTFA s. 74); FINTRAC may also seek civil penalties against individuals; travel restrictions can be imposed pending criminal prosecution.
